page: Hetzner Cloud cpx11 is an entry-level virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 2 shared vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 0.98 GB of RAM per core, and is equipped with 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the instance operates in the lower performance tiers. Both single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng place the server in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block reads and writes, consistently rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Passmark CPU and memory scores fall into the weak and poor categories, respectively. However, the server demonstrates average performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text generation using a small 135M parameter language model.

Given the shared CPU allocation and modest resource density, this server type is positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads with low resource demands. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage offers fast local I/O relative to the compute constraints, though the overall system is limited by its lower memory bandwidth and processing throughput. Appropriate workloads include lightweight utility tasks, basic text processing, small-scale development environments, and non-critical background services that do not require sustained high CPU utilization.
